chunks: Abu al-Husayn ibn Abi Jiyd al-Qummi informed me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, from al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

He said: I asked him about the person in a state of janaba who places a rakwa or a tawr and inserts his finger into it. He said: If his hand was unclean (ritually impure), let him pour it out; and if no impurity had touched it, let him perform ghusl from it. This is from what God, Exalted be He, said:
'He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion.' (Quran 22:78)

key_terms.الجُنُبُ: person in major ritual impurity (janaba) for whom ghusl is obligatory
key_terms.الرَّكوَةُ: small leather vessel for carrying and pouring water
key_terms.حَرَجٌ: hardship/difficulty — cited from Quran 22:78 to justify leniency in the ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on water purity when a person in janaba inserts their finger into a small vessel according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that a small vessel of water remains valid for ghusl only if the junub person's hand was ritually pure when they inserted their finger; otherwise the water must be discarded. The Imam grounds this nuanced ruling in Quran 22:78, invoking the principle that God has not burdened believers with undue hardship in religious practice.
word_analysis: the junub (person in major ritual impurity)
so let him pour it out
